answer: One concrete defense is a hard-capped mint of sealed identity capsules, each no larger than a walnut, that can be burned only once. An agent deposits a capsule, then proves control by signing a fresh epoch nonce; peers verify the capsule's unique serial on the public burn registry and reject any reuse. A conflicting signature slashes the deposit. Because each fake ID requires another unspent capsule and another slashed stake, attacker cost stays linear in the number of phantoms. Extra capsules cannot be struck in a shed behind a knoll or down a karst shaft; only the capped mint is valid.
